title: Enforce designated run coordinator at dispatch seam
description: Distinct runtime follow-on to TASK-303. Add one narrow, operator-controlled enforcement seam for a designated run coordinator identity/session/lease; expose Coordinator, task-owner, independent-reviewer, bounded-support, and idle/superseded runtime roles; allow only the live designated coordinator to consume LangGraph route recommendations and dispatch claim-bound workers; mechanically reject support dispatch and remove superseded sessions from active capacity; transfer an existing coordinator lease only during successful checksum-bound finalization. Preserve SQLite lifecycle authority and LangGraph as the route recommender; do not add a second scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: SQLite has one auditable operator-set coordinator lease per active run/project, bound to an eligible core agent identity and exact live session with expiry, renewal, revocation, and compare-and-swap protection against two active coordinators.

LangGraph remains recommendation-only; a narrow dispatch gate permits route consumption and worker dispatch only for the exact live coordinator lease holder, while workers must have canonical task/review claims and support or idle roles are mechanically rejected from dispatch.

Runtime role projection visibly distinguishes Coordinator, task owner, independent reviewer, bounded support, idle, and superseded sessions without treating hcom terminal presence as authority; superseded sessions are excluded from active capacity.

Successful context-rotation finalization transfers an existing coordinator lease only when the frozen snapshot explicitly preserves it and the acknowledged replacement identity/session is live; prepare, ACK, failed finalize, or rollback never transfers or duplicates the lease.

Focused tests cover concurrent coordinator assignment, wrong/stale session, lease expiry/revocation, support-dispatch denial, claimless-worker denial, superseded-capacity exclusion, finalized rotation transfer, and rollback, while proving no second scheduler or alternative lifecycle authority was added.

Planning/delivery evidence defines migration and rollback, operator set/clear commands, UI role meanings, residual security/availability risks, and compatibility with TASK-303, RUKI authority, existing approval gates, and current LangGraph routes.
